(4) There will be some increase in traffic noise as traffic increases in the project area. An increase in traffic noise is expected to occur whether the highway improvement is or is not built, and the "no-build" alternative may have somewhat higher traffic noise levels than would occur on the reconstructed highway. Higher traffic noise on the "no-build" alternative is probable because increased traffic congestion will result in low operating speeds, and low operating speeds are associated with higher noise emissions from heavy commercial vehicles.
(5) Highway drainage will be carried in closed drainage systems to discharge points in existing regional drain systems. No significant water quality impacts are anticipated.
(6) No significant impacts on social institutions in the area were identified as a result of project studies or circulating the draft EIS for review and comment.
(7) The improvement will provide an interface between transportation modes. Under a companion project a transportation center is being planned where FAP-23 crosses the Illinois Central-Gulf Railroad. The projects are being fully coordinated so that automobile park-n-ride facilities will be provided for rail mass transit users, and loading and transfer facilities will be provided for the exchange between bus and rail mass transit users. The highway improvement is an integral part of the overall planned transportation improvement.
The project studies recognize that highway no e will exceed the Noise Standards that were developed for highway projects. In most cases, it will not be possible to provide noise abatement because the properties adjacent to the highway are served by direct access to the highway through numerous driveways. Frequent openings in a noise barrier would render a noise barrier ineffective as a noise abatement device. Neither current Illinois law nor current Federal-aid highway regulations provide for installation of sound insulation devices on or in non-public buildings for noise abatement. Thus noise abatement methodology will be very difficult to apply to the improvement.
FHWA will require application of the Noise Standards where it is feasible and prudent to do so.
